description: This entry represents the ankyrin repeat-containing domain. These domains contain multiple repeats of a β(2)-α(2) motif. The ankyrin repeat is one of the most common protein-protein interaction motifs in nature. Ankyrin repeats are tandemly repeated modules of about 33 amino acids. They occur in a large number of functionally diverse proteins mainly from eukaryotes. The few known examples from prokaryotes and viruses may be the result of horizontal gene transfers [[cite:PUB00006219]]. The repeat has been found in proteins of diverse function such as transcriptional initiators, cell-cycle regulators, cytoskeletal, ion transporters and signal transducers. The ankyrin fold appears to be defined by its structure rather than its function since there is no specific sequence or structure which is universally recognised by it.

feature_name: Ankyrin Repeat and Cyclin-Dependent Kinase Inhibitor
description: The protein family includes ankyrin repeat domain-containing proteins and cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors. Ankyrin repeat proteins may play roles in cell division and other regulatory functions, while cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors are involved in cell cycle regulation by interacting with CDK4 and CDK6, inhibiting cell growth and proliferation. Some family members are involved in endosomal mRNA transport, chitinase secretion, and phosphoprotein substrate recognition. Others may act as substrate-recognition components of E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complexes, mediating ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of target proteins.
